title: The judges and the laws
summary: In the first year of the judges’ reign over the people of Nephi, Mosiah had died without leaving a successor. He had established laws that the people acknowledged and were obliged to obey.

explicit_facts.text: It was the first year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi.
King Mosiah had died, leaving none to reign in his stead.
Mosiah had established laws; the people acknowledged them and were obliged to abide by them.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the people and their surroundings.
How, if at all, the laws are represented visually.

narration.text: they were obliged to abide by the laws which he had made.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mosiah’s death and earlier acts are narrated background, not events to stage as happening in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Mosiah’s death as a present event or invent a successor.
Do not depict a specific act of law enforcement or compliance not described in the verse.

title: A Man Brought Before Alma
summary: In the first year of Alma's reign in the judgment-seat, a large man noted for his strength is brought before him to be judged. The man had previously preached among the people against the church and declared that priests and teachers ought to be popular, supported by the people, and not labor with their hands.

explicit_facts.text: In the first year of Alma's reign in the judgment-seat, a man was brought before him to be judged.
The man was large and noted for his strength.
The man had preached among the people against the church, calling his preaching the word of God.
He declared that priests and teachers ought to be popular, supported by the people, and not labor with their hands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and the man can be shown facing one another at the judgment-seat.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the judgment-seat, clothing, and any people who brought the man.

narration.text: there was a man brought before him to be judged

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The man's preaching is reported as a prior activity, not an event occurring at the judgment-seat.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the man or depict an invented trial procedure, dialogue, or a simultaneous preaching event.

title: Nehor's teaching draws support
summary: Nehor teaches his claims about salvation, and many believe him, support him, and give him money.

explicit_facts.text: Nehor taught that all mankind should be saved at the last day and have eternal life, and need not fear or tremble.
Many believed Nehor and began to support him and give him money.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nehor may be shown preaching to listeners who offer him money.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, audience size, clothing, and manner of giving money.

narration.text: all men should have eternal life.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The salvation claim is Nehor's teaching as reported by the narrator, not an endorsed doctrine.
prohibited_inventions: Do not represent the teaching as a visible miracle or divine event.

title: Pride and costly apparel
summary: A man grows proud, begins wearing costly apparel, and begins establishing a church after the manner of his preaching.

explicit_facts.text: He began to be lifted up in the pride of his heart.
He began to wear very costly apparel.
He began to establish a church after the manner of his preaching.

reasonable_visual_inferences: His costly apparel may be visible.
unspecified_visual_details: The apparel's design, the location, and how the church is established.

narration.text: And he began to be lifted up in the pride of his heart,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not describe the church as a building or identify the man by name.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the man, invent followers or a ceremony, or depict an unspecified church building as established fact.

title: Gideon Withstands an Unnamed Man
summary: An unnamed man, going to preach to those who believed his word, meets Gideon, a teacher in the church of God. The man contends sharply with Gideon, who withstands him and admonishes him with the words of God.

explicit_facts.text: The unnamed man was going to preach to those who believed his word when he met a teacher belonging to the church of God.
He contended sharply with the teacher to lead away the people of the church; the teacher withstood him, admonishing him with the words of God.
The teacher was Gideon, who had been an instrument in delivering the people of Limhi out of bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two men may be shown facing one another during their contention.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, and appearance of either man.

narration.text: but the man withstood him, admonishing him with the words of God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Gideon's role in the deliverance of Limhi's people is background, not an event occurring during this encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the unnamed man, invent words spoken in the dispute, or depict the earlier deliverance as part of this scene.

title: Gideon is slain
summary: Gideon withstands a man with the words of God. Angered, the man draws his sword and strikes Gideon. Gideon cannot withstand the blows because of his age and is slain.

explicit_facts.text: Gideon withstood the man with the words of God, and the man was angry with Gideon.
The man drew his sword and began to strike Gideon.
Gideon could not withstand the blows because of his many years and was slain by the sword.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sword attack can be shown without depicting wounds or blood.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the men's exact appearances are not stated.

narration.text: therefore he was slain by the sword.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not supply the words Gideon spoke.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the attacker from material outside the supplied verse.
Do not invent Gideon's spoken words.
Do not show wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: The man is brought before Alma
summary: The people of the church take the man who slew someone and bring him before Alma for judgment. He stands before Alma and pleads for himself with much boldness.

explicit_facts.text: The people of the church took the man who slew him and brought him before Alma to be judged according to his crimes.
The man stood before Alma and pleaded for himself with much boldness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The man may be shown facing Alma while he pleads.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the characters’ appearances are not described.

narration.text: And the man who slew him was taken by the people of the church, and was brought before Alma, to be judged according to the crimes which he had committed.
And it came to pass that he stood before Alma and pleaded for himself with much boldness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The words of the man's plea are not supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the man or the person he slew.
Do not invent the man's plea, other dialogue, or a specific judgment setting.

title: Alma condemns priestcraft
summary: Alma tells Nehor that he is guilty of priestcraft and tried to enforce it by the sword. Alma cites Gideon's death and condemns Nehor to die under Mosiah's law.

explicit_facts.text: Alma said this was the first introduction of priestcraft among the people and accused Nehor of trying to enforce it by the sword, warning of the people's destruction if priestcraft were enforced.
Alma said Nehor had shed the blood of a righteous man who had done much good, and that sparing him would bring the blood upon them for vengeance.
Alma condemned Nehor to die according to the law given by Mosiah and acknowledged by the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown addressing Nehor from the judgment seat.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the judgment seat and any audience.

spoken_dialogue.text: Therefore thou art condemned to die,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma the Younger (high priest)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's words are the judgment and explanation given in the supplied text.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent additional verdict proceedings or dialogue.

title: Nehor acknowledges his teaching
summary: Nehor is carried to the top of hill Manti, where he acknowledges between heaven and earth that his teaching was contrary to the word of God, and suffers an ignominious death.

explicit_facts.text: Nehor was carried to the top of hill Manti and acknowledged that what he had taught was contrary to the word of God; there he suffered an ignominious death.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nehor and those carrying him may be shown on the hilltop.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner of death and the appearance of those carrying him.

narration.text: what he had taught to the people was contrary to the word of God;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text does not describe the manner of death.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a specific execution method or depict gore.

title: Priestcraft continues
summary: Priestcraft continued to spread through the land. Many preached false doctrines for riches and honor. Fearing punishment under the law, they avoided known lies, theft, robbery, and murder, while professing to preach according to their beliefs.

explicit_facts.text: Priestcraft continued to spread through the land; many preached false doctrines for riches and honor.
They feared punishment for lies that would be known, pretended to preach according to their beliefs, and could not be punished by law for belief.
They feared punishment for theft and did not dare to rob or murder; murder was punishable by death.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Unnamed preachers addressing listeners could represent the reported spread of their teachings.
unspecified_visual_details: The preachers' appearances, the listeners, and the precise setting.

narration.text: they went forth preaching false doctrines; and this they did for the sake of riches and honor.
and now the law could have no power on any man for his belief.
neither durst they rob, nor murder, for he that murdered was punished unto death.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses report continuing conditions, not a particular sermon, crime, or trial.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific theft, robbery, murder, punishment, or trial.
Do not invent a preacher's words or name any member of the group.

title: Persecution of church members
summary: People who did not belong to the church of God began persecuting those who belonged to it and had taken upon themselves the name of Christ. They afflicted them with words because of their humility and their sharing of the word of God without payment.
characters: People who did not belong to the church of God
People who belonged to the church of God

explicit_facts.text: People who did not belong to the church of God began persecuting those who belonged to it and had taken upon themselves the name of Christ.
They afflicted church members with words because of their humility, their lack of pride, and their sharing of the word of God with one another without payment.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The groups may be shown facing one another, with gestures conveying verbal persecution.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, individuals' identities, and words spoken by the persecutors are unspecified.

narration.text: Yea, they did persecute them, and afflict them with all manner of words,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage describes affliction with words; it does not describe a physical attack.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent insults, dialogue, or physical violence.

title: Contention among church members
summary: Despite a law against persecution, many among the church members became proud and contended with their adversaries, striking one another with their fists. In the second year of Alma's reign, this caused the church much affliction and trial.

explicit_facts.text: A strict law forbade church members from persecuting nonmembers and forbade persecution among themselves.
Many among them became proud, contended warmly with their adversaries, and struck one another with their fists.
This occurred in the second year of Alma's reign and caused the church much affliction and trial.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The described blows can be shown without visible injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and identities of the people involved are not specified.

narration.text: they would smite one another with their fists.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The law provides context for the contention; no enforcement action is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named fighters, dialogue, injuries, or a specific location.

title: Withdrawal and steadfastness
summary: Many had hardened hearts, their names were blotted out, and many withdrew. Those who stood fast in the faith kept God's commandments and patiently bore persecution.
characters: Those who stood fast in the faith

explicit_facts.text: Many people's hearts were hardened, their names were blotted out, and they were remembered no more among the people of God.
Many withdrew themselves from among the people of God.
Those who stood fast in the faith kept God's commandments and patiently bore persecution.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Some people may be shown leaving a group while others remain.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and visible form of the persecution are not specified.
The manner in which names were blotted out is not specified.

narration.text: And also many withdrew themselves from among them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The blotted-out names are reported; the verses do not describe a visible erasure.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine hand or miraculous erasure.
Do not invent a specific act of persecution or dialogue.

title: Priests and people return to labor
summary: Priests leave their labor to teach, and the people leave their labor to hear. Afterward, all return diligently to their work, with preacher and hearer regarded as equals.
characters: Priests of the church of God
People hearing the word of God

explicit_facts.text: Priests left their labor to teach the word of God, and the people left their labors to hear; afterward all returned diligently to their labor.
The preacher was no better than the hearer and the teacher no better than the learner; all were equal and labored according to their strength.

unspecified_visual_details: The specific work, teaching place, and appearance of the people.

title: Sharing with those in need
summary: They impart their substance according to what each has to the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted. They do not wear costly apparel but are neat and comely. They establish the affairs of the church and begin to have continual peace again despite persecutions.
characters: The poor, needy, sick, and afflicted

explicit_facts.text: They imparted their substance according to what each had to the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted.
They did not wear costly apparel, yet were neat and comely.
They established the affairs of the church and began to have continual peace again despite persecutions.

unspecified_visual_details: The goods shared, clothing designs, and setting.

title: Abundance among the church
summary: Because of the church's steadiness, they became exceedingly rich and had abundant goods. In their prosperity, they did not send away people in need and were liberal to all without respect to persons.

explicit_facts.text: Because of the steadiness of the church, they became exceedingly rich and had abundant flocks, herds, fatlings, grain, gold, silver, precious things, silk, fine-twined linen, and homely cloth.

They did not send away those who were naked, hungry, thirsty, sick, or not nourished; they did not set their hearts upon riches and were liberal to all in need without respect to age, status, sex, or church membership.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abundant goods and people in need may be shown together.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, people's appearances, and arrangement of the goods are not specified.

they were liberal to all, both old and young, both bond and free, both male and female

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The abundance and generosity are reported conditions, not a specified single encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a named recipient, a specific distribution event, or a location.
Do not portray the wealth as a divine reward beyond what the verses state.

title: Prosperity, law, and peace
summary: Those belonging to the church prospered and became wealthier than those outside it. The text describes wrongdoing among nonmembers and enforcement of the law where possible. People became more still, and peace lasted among the people of Nephi until the fifth year of the reign of the judges.

explicit_facts.text: Those belonging to the church prospered and became wealthier than those who did not belong to it.
The text attributes various forms of wrongdoing to those outside the church and says the law was enforced on transgressors as far as possible.

As the law was exercised, people suffered according to their deeds, became more still, and dared not commit known wickedness. There was much peace among the people of Nephi until the fifth year of the reign of the judges.
